content: A pelvic examination, also known as a pelvic exam, is a clinical evaluation of the female pelvic organs. It is typically divided into two components: the external examination and the internal examination. In certain situations, the presence of a chaperone may be appropriate. External Examination: The external examination involves an assessment of the external anatomy of the female genitalia. The clinician evaluates the skin for any lesions, abnormalities, or signs of infection. Internal Examination: A speculum is used to visualize the external cervical os and assess the vaginal walls and cervix. The clinician examines for the presence of any foreign bodies within the vaginal canal. Manoeuvres Performed During the Internal Examination: The clinician tests for cervical motion tenderness, which is a hallmark finding in conditions such as pelvic inflammatory disease. Palpation of the adnexal structures, including the ovaries and fallopian tubes, is performed to assess for masses, tenderness, or abnormalities. Cervical swabs are taken to test for sexually transmitted infections or other pathogens. Vaginal swabs are collected for microbiological analysis or other diagnostic purposes. A Pap smear is performed to screen for cervical dysplasia or malignancy.
